imp0.title: Annual Community Interaction and Shared Participation Survey (park users and residents)
imp0.indicator: % of surveyed participants reporting that the park provides increased opportunities for interaction and shared community participation between Syrian refugees and the host community
imp0.who: Enumerator appointed by the Municipality, or a focal point from a local association, supervised by the municipal community coordinator
imp0.when: Annually (one round per year, 2027 / 2028 / 2029), after the main activity season
imp0.calc: (No. of respondents answering 'Strongly agree' or 'Agree' to Q15 ÷ total respondents who visited the park at least once in the last 12 months) × 100. Report alongside Q13, Q14, Q16 and Q19 as supporting evidence.
imp0.disaggregation: Sex; age group; nationality / status; disability; neighbourhood
imp0.definition: Evidence from participant feedback, activity records and municipal observations showing that park activities create opportunities for members of both communities to participate together.
imp0.measures: Whether residents from the host community and the Syrian refugee community are actually present together in the park, interact there, take part in joint activities, and perceive the park as having increased opportunities for shared participation.
imp0.unit: one surveyed resident or park user
imp0.source: Activity feedback forms, attendance records, municipal reports, annual resident survey
imp0.evidence: Completed questionnaires; sampling note; event attendance records for the period; annual survey summary signed by the community coordinator

so10.title: Annual Partner Coordination and Collaboration Survey
so10.indicator: % of partner organisations reporting effective coordination and collaboration with the Municipality in implementing park activities
so10.who: Municipal community coordinator / liaison officer (self-administered by the partner where possible)
so10.when: Annually — all partners on the stakeholder map with at least one documented interaction during the year
so10.calc: (No. of partner organisations selecting 'Strongly agree' or 'Agree' on Q14 ÷ total partner organisations surveyed) × 100. Target ≥ 70%. Q9–Q13 reported as a sub-index.
so10.disaggregation: Partner type; sex of respondent where applicable
so10.definition: Share of surveyed partner organisations reporting that coordination, communication and joint planning with the Municipality improved during implementation of the Action Plan.
so10.measures: Partner-side experience of the partnership mechanism: clarity of roles, timeliness of communication, involvement in joint planning, follow-up on decisions, transparency in recording contributions, and whether coordination improved over the year.
so10.unit: one partner organisation (one response per organisation per year)
so10.source: Short annual partner survey or structured interviews; stakeholder map as the sampling frame
so10.evidence: Completed partner questionnaires; stakeholder map used as the sampling frame; interview notes; annual coordination summary

a1.title: Milestone Verification Checklist — Municipal Partnership Mechanism Established
a1.who: Municipal community coordinator, countersigned by the Executive Director or the Mayor
a1.when: First verification within six months of Plan adoption; reviewed annually thereafter
a1.calc: Simple count — one mechanism established. Status = 'Established' only when items 4, 7, 10 and 11 are all recorded 'In place'; otherwise 'Partly established' or 'Not established'.
a1.definition: A functioning coordination arrangement including a designated municipal focal point, stakeholder list, partner communication arrangements, and contribution tracking.
a1.measures: Whether each of the four constituent components of the mechanism exists in documented form and is in use, plus the supporting steps set out in the Action Plan (requirements list, introductory meetings, periodic updates, Council endorsement).
a1.unit: one verification exercise (within six months of Plan adoption, then reviewed annually)
a1.source: Municipal records: appointment decision, stakeholder map, requirements list, contribution register, meeting minutes, Council decisions
a1.evidence: Copies of the appointment decision and terms of reference; stakeholder map file; rehabilitation requirements list; contribution register extract; minutes of introductory meetings; Council decision; signed checklist

a2.indicator: Number of coordination meetings held with partners
a2.who: Municipal community coordinator / liaison officer (rapporteur of the meeting)
a2.when: Completed after every meeting, throughout the implementation period
a2.calc: Cumulative count of documented meetings. Target ≥ 4 per year (≥ 12 over the Plan period). Count only meetings where Q18 = 'Yes, prepared and filed'.
a2.disaggregation: By partner type (association / cultural / private sector / educational / government / donor)
a2.definition: Meetings conducted with community organisations, cultural institutions, schools, businesses and other relevant partners, documented through minutes or attendance records.
a2.measures: Each countable meeting and its documentation quality: who convened it, which partner types attended, what was decided, what was assigned, and whether minutes and an attendance sheet exist. A meeting without minutes or an attendance sheet is not counted.
a2.source: Meeting minutes and signed attendance sheets held by the community coordinator
a2.evidence: Signed minutes; signed attendance sheet with organisation names; agenda; photographs where appropriate; follow-up action table

a3.title: Partner Contribution Record (financial, in-kind, technical and volunteer support)
a3.indicator: Value and type of contributions mobilised from partners
a3.who: Municipal community coordinator, with the Directorate of Financial Affairs for received goods and cash
a3.when: Completed at the time of each pledge or receipt; reviewed and totalled annually
a3.calc: Simple record of contributions received. Report the annual total value in JOD by contribution type and by source type. Count only records with status 'Received' or 'Partly received' in the value total; report pledges separately.
a3.definition: Financial, in-kind, technical or volunteer contributions supporting park rehabilitation and activities.
a3.measures: Each contribution separately: who gave it, what exactly was given, its estimated value and how that value was derived, which Plan activity and which item on the rehabilitation requirements list it covers, and whether it was formally received and acknowledged.
a3.source: Contribution register maintained by the Municipality; receipts, delivery notes, letters, MoUs and volunteer attendance sheets
a3.evidence: Delivery note or receipt; photographs of delivered items; contributor letter or MoU; volunteer attendance sheet for labour contributions; municipal acceptance decision

b1.title: Milestone Verification Checklist — Park Use and Activity Arrangements Established
b1.indicator: Park use and activity arrangements established
b1.who: Municipal community coordinator, countersigned by the Executive Director
b1.when: First verification within the first year of implementation; reviewed annually
b1.calc: Simple count — one operational arrangement established and updated as needed. Status = 'Established' when items 3, 4, 6, 7 and 8 are all 'In place'.
b1.definition: Basic arrangements developed for park use, including activity scheduling, use of spaces, coordination procedures, and communication with partners.
b1.measures: Whether the operational protocol foreseen by the Plan exists and is applied: a written arrangement approved by the Municipality, a published activity calendar, a request procedure for community organisations, defined spaces and permitted uses, the non-commercial rule, equitable access and accessibility provisions, maintenance and supervision responsibilities, and a feedback channel.
b1.unit: one verification exercise (within the first year, then reviewed annually)
b1.source: Municipal records and the activity calendar; approved operational protocol; Council decisions
b1.evidence: Approved operational protocol and its Council decision; activity calendar; blank request form; site layout plan; copies of public notices; feedback log; signed checklist

so20.title: Park User Satisfaction and Activity Feedback Form (short exit form)
so20.indicator: % of surveyed park users satisfied with the park as a safe and welcoming shared community space
so20.who: Activity organiser or a volunteer assigned to feedback collection, supervised by the community coordinator
so20.when: At each activity on a sample of participants; aggregated and reported annually
so20.calc: (No. of respondents selecting 'Very satisfied' or 'Satisfied' on Q9 ÷ total respondents surveyed) × 100. Target ≥ 60%. Q10–Q13 reported as the supporting dimension scores.
so20.disaggregation: Sex; age group; nationality / status; disability
so20.definition: Participants providing positive feedback on the suitability of activities and on the park as a shared community space.
so20.measures: Satisfaction with the park as a shared space, broken into the dimensions that make it one: sense of safety, feeling welcome regardless of origin, suitability for women and children, condition of the facilities including accessibility, and suitability of the activity attended.
so20.unit: one participant at one activity or visit
so20.source: Short feedback forms or verbal feedback records collected at activities
so20.evidence: Completed feedback forms or the verbal feedback log; the activity record they relate to; the aggregation sheet used for annual reporting

c1.title: Park Rehabilitation Works Completion Record
c1.who: Engineering Services Department with the community coordinator; volunteer-delivered items verified by the municipal supervisor
c1.when: Completed for each item during the rehabilitation phase (first six months: June–November 2026), and for any later improvement
c1.calc: Simple count against the agreed rehabilitation list: number of items with status 'Completed' ÷ number of items on the priority list. Report the count of completed items by facility type.
c1.definition: Rehabilitation or improvement works completed in the designated park section, including seating, play areas, landscaping, sports facilities, lighting, accessibility features and other agreed improvements.
c1.measures: Completion of each item on the agreed rehabilitation priority list: what was done, where, quantity, how it was delivered and resourced, whether it meets accessibility requirements, whether it passed a safety check, and whether it was handed over for public use.
c1.unit: one improvement item on the agreed rehabilitation list
c1.source: Site inspection and completion records; the rehabilitation requirements list prepared under KHLD-SO1-A1
c1.evidence: Before and after photographs; completion note or engineer's report; delivery notes for materials; safety inspection note; handover record

permit.label: Municipal approval or permit reference and date

stalls_offered.label: Number of stalls or spaces made available

stalls_occupied.label: Number of stalls actually occupied
stalls_occupied.help: Must equal the number of vendors present on form 22.

announcement.label: How and when was the opportunity to participate announced?
announcement.help: The Plan requires that opportunities be announced publicly and transparently.

applications.label: Number of applications received and number accepted

selection_method.label: How were vendors selected?
selection_method.help: Mitigation for the risk of perceived inequitable access.

priority_share.label: Number of accepted vendors from priority groups

fee_charged.label: Was any fee charged to vendors for a stall?
fee_charged.help: The Plan defines the park as non-commercial; any fee must be justified, authorised and reported to the Municipality.

parts.fee_charged: No — free of charge / Yes — fee

fee_charged.false: No — stalls provided free of charge

refreshment_point.label: Did a community organisation operate a snack or refreshment point?
refreshment_point.help: Permitted under the Plan where applicable procedures allow.

services_provided.label: Which services were provided to vendors?
services_provided.help: Vendor feedback on facilities is collected on form 18.

accessibility.label: Was the market area accessible to persons with disabilities and to mothers with prams?

visitors.label: Estimated number of visitors and how it was estimated
visitors.help: Also record on form 12 if the market was counted as a community activity.

hygiene_check.label: Was a hygiene and food safety check carried out on food stalls?
hygiene_check.help: Vendors commit to hygiene and fair pricing standards under the Plan.

parallel_activities.label: Which activities were held alongside the market?
parallel_activities.help: Record each separately on form 11 where it is a distinct activity.

total_sales.label: Estimated total sales reported by vendors (JOD) and how the figure was obtained
total_sales.help: Report as vendor-reported, never as verified income.

cost.label: Cost of organising the market and source of funds
cost.help: Annex 1 of the Plan indicates about JOD 2,000 per market.

feedback_collected.label: Was feedback collected from vendors and visitors?
feedback_collected.help: Vendor follow-up is conducted on form 18 (KHLD-SO4-0).

lessons.label: Lessons learned to apply at the next market day

recorded_by.label: Record completed by and verified by (names, positions, dates)

h2.title: Market Day Vendor Registration Sheet (one entry per vendor per market day)
h2.indicator: Number of home-based enterprises and vendors participating in park hosted seasonal markets
h2.who: Registration desk staffed by the Municipality and the co-organising local association
h2.when: On every market day, starting from April 2027
h2.calc: Count of registered vendors per market (participations), and a unique count of vendor IDs across all markets. Target 100–150 vendor participations.
h2.disaggregation: Sex; age group including youth 15–24; nationality (Jordanian / Syrian refugee); disability; product type
h2.definition: Household producers and home-based businesses occupying a stall or space in at least one market day. Both total participations and unique vendors are tracked, with priority for under-represented groups per the Plan (women, low-income families, youth, refugees, persons with disabilities).
h2.measures: Each vendor at each market day, with a stable vendor ID so that total participations and unique vendors can both be reported, the full disaggregation the framework requires, the priority-group flags, and the licensing and hygiene status of the activity.
h2.unit: one vendor at one market day
h2.source: Vendor registration sheets completed at each market day
h2.evidence: Signed registration sheet; stall allocation plan; hygiene and fair-pricing commitment signed by food vendors; copies of licences or health certificates where held

market_id.label: Market reference number and date (must match form 21)

returning_vendor.label: Has this vendor participated in a previous market day under the Plan?
returning_vendor.help: This is what separates total participations from the unique vendor count.
returning_vendor.sub: No — new vendor, assign a new vendor ID | Yes — existing vendor ID

enterprise_id.label: Enterprise ID, if the vendor is already in the enterprise support log
enterprise_id.help: Links this sheet to forms 19 and 20.
enterprise_id.sub: KHLD-ENT- | Not in the support log

id_number.label: National ID number, or UNHCR registration number for Syrian refugees
id_number.help: Collected only for unique counting; see the guidance sheet.

dob_age.label: Date of birth and age (used to derive the age band)
dob_age.sub: Date of birth Age Youth 15–24: Yes / No

disability.label: Do you have difficulty doing any of the following: seeing, hearing, walking or climbing steps, remembering or concentrating, self-care, communicating?
disability.help: If a difficulty is reported, note any adjustment needed at the stall.

priority_flags.label: Priority group flags under the Plan's participation criteria
priority_flags.help: Basis for reporting that priority was given to under-represented groups.

vendor_type.label: Type of vendor
vendor_type.help: Required for reporting home-based enterprises separately from other vendors.

product_categories.label: Product categories offered at this market day

licensed.label: Is the activity licensed or registered?
licensed.help: Unlicensed vendors are referred to the guidance sessions (form 19).

health_certificate.label: For food products: does the vendor hold a health certificate or food safety approval?
health_certificate.help: Record the status; do not exclude a vendor solely on this basis without a municipal decision.

first_organised_market.label: Is this the vendor's first time participating in an organised market or exhibition?

nominated_by.label: How did the vendor come to participate?

stall_free.label: Was the stall provided free of charge?
stall_free.help: Must be consistent with the fee question on form 21.

parts.stall_free: Yes — free of charge / No — fee paid

equipment_provided.label: Equipment provided by the organisers to this vendor

commitment_signed.label: Has the vendor signed the commitment to hygiene, safety and fair pricing standards?
commitment_signed.help: Required of participating producers under the Plan.

attended.label: Did the vendor actually attend on the day?
attended.help: Only vendors who attended count towards the indicator.

sales_band.label: Approximate sales on the day (optional, asked at the end of the market)
sales_band.help: Voluntary; feeds the total sales figure on form 21 and the follow-up survey on form 18.

consent.label: Does the vendor consent to their details being kept in the municipal producer register and to being contacted for a follow-up survey, and to photographs being used in municipal reports?
consent.help: Consent to recontact is what makes indicator KHLD-SO4-0 possible.

dashboard.intro: Twenty-one indicators from the Al Khalidiyah results framework, computed from the twenty-one forms. Every figure is read from the database; nothing is typed or worked out here.
dashboard.planTargetNote: The Plan states targets for the whole period, by year or as a percentage; none is split into quarters. The quarterly column therefore reads "not set", never zero.

rules.title: Milestone rules
rules.intro: Each milestone form carries a rule naming the checklist items that must be "In place" for the milestone to count as established. Two of the four name items that are not checklist rows, so their status cannot be computed until a coordinator writes the critical items here. The sheet's own rule is shown verbatim; the decision is data, and the indicator views read it on the next query.
rules.chooseItems: Tick the checklist items that must all be "In place".
rules.boundary: Established when every critical item is In place; Not established when none is In place or Partly in place; Partly established otherwise (plan §7.3, a default for the M&E lead to confirm).
